transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Jordan Blake (CTO, Helios), Samira Khan (Head of ML), Evan Li (Infra), Rita Mendoza (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Discussed Dedicated capacity tradeoffs and audit logs. Agreed next steps and pilot.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Liam (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Liam, AE on the account, and Priya is our solutions engineer, she'll run the console demo. Maya will follow up on onboarding and CSM logistics.
00:18 Jordan (Helios): Thanks Liam. we'll try to keep this focused, Samira is mainly interested in the per-route cost breakdowns and how we can attribute token cost by endpoint. Evan and Rita are here for infra and security.
00:32 Priya (Redwood): Great. I'll share my screen - let me know if the stream looks ok. We're on the Console -> Usage Analytics page. You'll see high-level usage trends, and then per-route breakdowns that you can pivot by model, route, and time window.
00:58 Priya (Redwood): So here is a sample customer with three routes: triage-chat, summarization-batch, and embeddings-search. Each route shows tokens in, tokens out, requests, p95 latency and estimated cost based on your pricing profile. Note the little info icon - that uses our cost model which factors in model type, quantization, and batching efficiency.
01:25 Samira (Helios): Quick question - how accurate is that estimated cost? we run some batched offline jobs so the per-token cost is different for embeddings.
01:34 Priya (Redwood): Good call. the console shows an estimated cost using the active profile; for Dedicated fleets you can upload adjusted kernel/quantization factors - that updates the estimator. For embeddings vs generation we separate compute vs storage units; batching heuristics may make the estimator off by ~5-15% depending on profile.
01:55 Jordan (Helios): Is that estimator adjustable per-customer? we have internal rates for certain models if we go Dedicated.
02:03 Liam (Redwood): Yes, we maintain account-level pricing overrides. we'll include dedicated capacity pricing in the spreadsheet - you can see both hosted list and committed rates.
02:12 Evan (Helios): And the latency numbers - are those end-to-end including network hops? or just server-side?
02:18 Priya (Redwood): The p95/p99 on the dashboard are server-side plus Redwood ingress egress; we also show synthetic SLA monitors if you add them. You can toggle to show total end-to-end by piping in your app-side traces.
02:32 Rita (Helios): For security, we need audit logs with prompt hashes, model id, route, user_id, and request timestamps. also retention controls.
02:44 Maya (Redwood): We have an audit/export page and S3 delivery for logs; SOC 2 packet includes which fields are available. Priya will share the schema after the call.
02:55 Priya (Redwood): Switching to the per-route dashboard: here's triage-chat. It shows request volume by minute, average tokens per request, and a cost waterfall - model compute, kv-cache hit savings, and batching delta. Note the annotations for cache hit rate - we surface prefix cache effectiveness which can reduce per-token cost materially.
03:22 Samira (Helios): We saw something about K V cache on your docs - is that the same as our KV cache? sometimes the docs say K-V cash and it's confusing in the transcript...
03:32 Priya (Redwood): (laughs) yeah the auto-transcripts sometimes do that. KV cache - key-value cache - is used for repeating prefixes. For streaming chat it helps keep token spend down.
03:40 Jordan (Helios): Walk us through the cost breakdown for that route - I want to see how the triage-chat compares to summarization-batch.
03:48 Priya (Redwood): Sure. On the right, cost by model shows: redwood-llama-70b (quantized) at 60% of compute spend, hosted-claude-style at 25%, and open embeddings at 15%. Then the per-request waterfall breaks into base model compute, batching savings, and cache savings. You can export this as CSV.
04:10 Evan (Helios): When you say quantized, does that mean we lose quality? Samira is worried about hallucinations in triage flow.
04:18 Samira (Helios): yes hallucination risk is a concern; what's the recommended tradeoff?
04:23 Priya (Redwood): We typically recommend using quantized variants for high-throughput non-critical routes, and full float variants for sensitive triage. Redwood Optimize can give model recommendations per route; we can run an eval set to measure metric regressions before you flip.
04:40 Liam (Redwood): We can also do canary rollouts - keep a small percentage on full-fp model and degrade slowly. The console has rollout controls.
04:50 Jordan (Helios): Good. can you show cost attribution by team or product? Our finance wants to allocate spend to business units.
04:58 Priya (Redwood): Yep - group by tag. You can tag routes with product_team: "CareOps" and then the dashboard aggregates by tag. The billing export includes tags so accounting can ingest it.
05:12 Rita (Helios): For compliance: SSO/SAML integration and RBAC? We need role separation, and the ability to scrub user-level PII from logs before sending to S3.
05:23 Maya (Redwood): We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access. For logs you can choose masked or hashed prompt storage and toggle retention window. We'll send our security packet which shows these options.
05:34 Jordan (Helios): Competitors - we've looked at Anthropic and an internal Databricks approach. how do you position on cost transparency?
05:42 Liam (Redwood): Our differentiator is per-route unit economics surfaced in the console - it's built to show you the knobs (batching, kv-cache, quantization) and the modeled cost impact. We'll also help tune configs with Redwood Optimize to hit target spend/loss thresholds.
05:58 Samira (Helios): Quick nit: can we see per-customer or per-end-user breakdown for multi-tenant usage?
06:06 Priya (Redwood): Yes, request-level metadata is available if you pass a customer_id header. We show top-k users by spend and alerts for unusual spend spikes.
06:16 Jordan (Helios): Alright, demo the alerting - say a sudden cost spike or latency regression.
06:22 Priya (Redwood): In Alerts -> you can set thresholds on p95 or daily spend per route. Example: triage-chat alert when daily compute increases 20% week-over-week. You get webhook or PagerDuty.
06:34 Evan (Helios): How do you calculate the cost delta? is it comparing to baseline or absolute?
06:38 Priya (Redwood): It's a configurable baseline - you can pick moving-average window or fixed baseline. The UI shows both absolute delta and percentage and breakdown by model contribution.
06:50 Jordan (Helios): Let's talk through a sample calculation - assume 100k requests/day, avg tokens in 120, tokens out 80, model A cost X - can you run that quickly?
07:01 Priya (Redwood): Yep I'll use the calculator. So with 100k requests, total tokens processed would be ~20M tokens/day. With model A at $0.0001 per token that equals $2k/day; with batching and a 20% cache-hit effective saving you'd be down to $1.4k. These are illustrative. We'll run precise numbers in the pilot.
07:26 Samira (Helios): Do you support per-route custom batching configs? embedding jobs we batch aggressively, chat routes not so much.
07:33 Priya (Redwood): Yes, batching policy is per-route. You can set max batch size, max latency, and burst policy. Console recommends values based on observed latency/throughput.
07:45 Jordan (Helios): On routing - we have a mix of latency-sensitive and throughput tasks. Is hybrid routing (hosted for low sensitivity, Dedicated for low-latency) straightforward?
07:54 Liam (Redwood): Absolutely. You can set routing policies by route, region, and confidence. If Dedicated is down, we have fallback to hosted models. We'll show that in docs.
08:08 Rita (Helios): For Dedicated, where does key management live? we require HSM-backed keys for patient data.
08:16 Maya (Redwood): Private and Dedicated support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and customer-controlled VPC peering. We'll attach the network diagram in the security packet.
08:28 Samira (Helios): Any gotchas for on-prem or air-gapped?
08:32 Priya (Redwood): There are packaging steps, and you'll need to allocate GPU resources for the Dedicated runtime; performance tuning matters. We'll provide a runbook.
08:44 Jordan (Helios): Ok back to the console, show me the export flows and the CSV format.
08:50 Priya (Redwood): Export -> choose time window -> format: CSV or JSONL. fields include timestamp, route, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_ms, cost_estimate, tags, request_id. We'll attach a sample CSV after the call.
09:08 Samira (Helios): Great. can you also show the per-model latency distribution? the p50/p95/p99 view?
09:14 Priya (Redwood): Yep on the model tab, here's p50/p95 with heatmap by time of day. You can drill into individual requests to see the prompt and model response (if not redacted).
09:30 Jordan (Helios): We need to redact PHI in logs - how does Redwood handle that?
09:36 Maya (Redwood): You can enable automatic redaction on ingestion or mask fields. We'll include details in the security packet and options for customer-side pre-hash before sending.
09:48 Evan (Helios): Pilot scope - we want to run triage-chat through Redwood for one week with production-like traffic and compare cost/latency with our current in-house infra. what's the expected onboarding time?
09:58 Liam (Redwood): For a pilot we usually do a 2-3 day setup for routing and keys, then a week of traffic. We'll coordinate with your infra for keys and SAML. Priya will own the technical onboarding and Maya will own the CSM tasks.
10:12 Samira (Helios): Success criteria - p95 latency < 450ms and cost <= 20% above internal in the pilot. We'll provide baseline metrics.
10:22 Liam (Redwood): Perfect - add that to the pilot doc.
10:26 Priya (Redwood): Quick note on Optimize: after the pilot we can run Optimize to recommend batching/quantization profiles to meet cost targets with minimal quality loss. It ties to the console so you'll see recommendations per-route.
10:40 Jordan (Helios): Any risk of quality regressions with quantization? we need to track a prompt-based evaluation set.
10:46 Priya (Redwood): We support per-route evals and regression alerts. You can upload a set of prompts and reference outputs; Optimize will score candidate configurations and warn if metric falls below threshold.
10:58 Rita (Helios): send SOC2, network diagram, and audit log schema. We want to review before pilot provisioning.
11:06 Liam (Redwood): Will do - I'll include the security packet and a pointer to the shared drive.
11:12 Jordan (Helios): Last thing - can you include a line item for canary rollouts and auto-fallback costs in the pricing?
11:20 Liam (Redwood): Yes, canary rollouts don't have extra fees but any extra duplicate traffic to hosted for fallback will count as usage; we'll show a scenario in the pricing doc.
11:28 Samira (Helios): ok thanks, that was thorough. we'll review and get back on dates for the pilot.
11:34 Liam (Redwood): Thanks everyone. Recap: Liam to send pricing and Dedicated options; Priya to share per-route CSV + sample alerts; Maya to send onboarding checklist and security packet; Helios to confirm pilot criteria and timeline.
11:50 Jordan (Helios): Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
